Q1
Both attributes are needed, so (B, F) is minimal and is the only candidate key. The prime attributes are B and F.
b) R is not in 3NF. Take the non-trivial dependency A -> CD. The determinant A is not a superkey of R, and neither C nor D is a prime attribute, because the only prime attributes are B and F. The 3NF test therefore fails for A -> CD, so R is only in 1NF as it stands.
c) R is not in BCNF because A -> CD and F -> A have determinants that are not superkeys.
In R2 the dependency F -> A still has a non-superkey determinant because F+ within R2 is {F, A, E} and does not contain B, so decompose again: R2a(B, F) with primary key (B, F) and R2b(F, A, E) with primary key F.
e) Lossless join: for R -> R1, R2 the intersection is {A} and A -> CD determines R1, so the binary decomposition is lossless. For R2 -> R2a, R2b the intersection is {F} and F -> AE determines R2b, so that step is also lossless, and composing the two steps gives a lossless join of the three relations.

Question 2
a) Accept.
b) The code uses a PreparedStatement, obtained from connObj.prepareStatement(query). The question marks are parameter placeholders; the values are supplied afterwards with setString or setInt, and the SQL text is compiled once by the driver so it can be executed again with different values.
c) A full backup copies all the data, all the objects and the transaction log, and it can be restored completely on its own. A differential or incremental backup copies only the data pages that have changed since the last full backup, so it is small and fast, and it must be restored together with its base full backup. A third type is the transaction log backup, which records every transaction since the previous log backup and allows recovery to a point in time. c) Full backup copies everything including the log and can be restored on its own. An incremental backup copies only the data changed since the last full backup.
d) A job is a set of steps run by SQL Server Agent and a schedule says when it runs, for example every night at 02:00. It is useful for unattended work such as a nightly backup or reindexing. d) A job is a task and a schedule is the time for it. It runs at the scheduled time.
I answered the parts as a, b, c and d using the terms PreparedStatement, backup, job and schedule.

Question 3
i) CREATE LOGIN Kasuni WITH PASSWORD = 'K@$uni2022';
ii) ALTER SERVER ROLE [sysadmin] ADD MEMBER [Kasuni]; sysadmin is the fixed server role that has authority over all administrative tasks on the server, such as CREATE DATABASE, CREATE LOGIN and changing server settings. Membership is added with ALTER SERVER ROLE ... ADD MEMBER and can be removed the same way.
iii) CREATE SERVER ROLE [SchoolDBManager] AUTHORIZATION [dbo]; creates the user defined server role. ALTER SERVER ROLE [SchoolDBManager] ADD MEMBER [saman.a]; then adds the login saman.a to it, and ALTER SERVER ROLE [SchoolDBManager] ADD MEMBER [Kasuni]; lets Kasuni hand out membership. Finally USE SchoolDB; and ALTER ROLE [SchoolDBManager] ADD MEMBER [saman.a]; give the role inside the database.
iv) USE SchoolDB; CREATE USER [thusitha.p] FOR LOGIN [thusitha.p]; maps the login into the database first. GRANT CREATE TABLE, CREATE VIEW, CREATE PROCEDURE, CREATE FUNCTION, CREATE TRIGGER TO [thusitha.p]; then gives exactly the DDL permissions Thusitha needs. She is deliberately not made a db_owner, because db_owner would also let her drop the database.
v) CREATE USER [Lasantha.h] FOR LOGIN [Lasantha.h]; GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA :: dbo TO [Lasantha.h]; GRANT EXECUTE ON SCHEMA :: dbo TO [Lasantha.h]; v) GRANT SELECT TO Lasantha.h;

Q4
a)(i) SELECT O.OID, C.name FROM "Order" O JOIN Customer C ON O.CID = C.CID WHERE C.gender = 'F' AND C.address LIKE '%France%'; a)(i) Order is a reserved keyword, so it must be written as "Order" in standard SQL. The join is on the foreign key CID and the two filters select female customers whose address contains France.
a)(ii) SELECT CID FROM Customer WHERE CID NOT IN (SELECT O.CID FROM "Order" O JOIN OrderItems OI ON O.OID = OI.OID JOIN Product P ON OI.PID = P.PID JOIN Manufacturer M ON P.MID = M.MID WHERE P.name = 'phones' AND M.country = 'India'); a)(ii) This is a set difference. NOT EXISTS with a correlated subquery would be safer than NOT IN, because NOT IN returns no rows at all if the subquery ever produces a NULL CID.
a)(iii) The subquery aggregates the quantities per order and keeps only the orders above the threshold with HAVING, because the condition applies to the group and not to a single row. SUM must be repeated in HAVING since the alias cannot be used there in standard SQL.
b) CREATE FUNCTION dbo.TotalPrice(@OID char(10)) RETURNS int AS BEGIN DECLARE @total int; SELECT @total = SUM(P.unitPrice * OI.qty) FROM OrderItems OI JOIN Product P ON OI.PID = P.PID WHERE OI.OID = @OID; RETURN ISNULL(@total, 0); END;
c) CREATE TRIGGER trgPackageWeight ON OrderItems AFTER INSERT, UPDATE AS BEGIN SET NOCOUNT ON; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM OrderItems OI JOIN Product P ON OI.PID = P.PID WHERE OI.OID IN (SELECT OID FROM inserted) GROUP BY OI.OID HAVING SUM(P.weight * OI.qty) > 2000) BEGIN RAISERROR('Package weight cannot exceed 2kg', 16, 1); ROLLBACK TRANSACTION; END END;

Student ID: IT21230104

Question 1
a) Attribute closure. B+ = {B, E}, so B alone is not a key. F+ = {F, A, C, D}, so F alone is not a key either. Starting from BF, the closure grows as BF+ = {B,F}; F -> A adds A giving {A,B,F}; A -> CD adds C and D giving {A,B,C,D,F}; B -> E adds E, so BF+ = {A,B,C,D,E,F} = R. Both attributes are needed, so (B, F) is minimal and is the only candidate key. The prime attributes are B and F.
b) R is not in 3NF because A -> CD has a determinant that is not a superkey and CD contains non-prime attributes.
c) R is not in BCNF either. BCNF requires the determinant of every non-trivial dependency to be a superkey. A -> CD has determinant A, and A+ = {A, C, D} is a proper subset of R, so this dependency violates BCNF. The same reasoning applies to F -> A, whose determinant F is not a superkey once the relation is decomposed. R is not in BCNF, A is not a key.
d) Decompose on A -> CD: R1(A, C, D) and R2(A, B, E, F). R1 has primary key A and is in BCNF. In R2 the dependency F -> A still has a non-superkey determinant because F+ within R2 is {F, A, E} and does not contain B, so decompose again: R2a(B, F) with primary key (B, F) and R2b(F, A, E) with primary key F. R2a has no non-trivial dependency at all and R2b has only F -> AE, where F is the key, so R1, R2a and R2b are all in BCNF.
e) Lossless join: for R -> R1, R2 the intersection is {A} and A -> CD determines R1, so the binary decomposition is lossless. For R2 -> R2a, R2b the intersection is {F} and F -> AE determines R2b, so that step is also lossless, and composing the two steps gives a lossless join of the three relations. e) Dependency preservation: A -> CD is checked entirely inside R1, and B -> E and F -> A are checked entirely inside R2b, so no join is required to verify any dependency of the original set.

Q2
a) The statement is accepted. A Type 2 JDBC driver is vendor specific and is only partly written in Java; the rest is native code that talks to the vendor client library, so the vendor driver must be installed and configured on every client machine. This is the difference from a Type 4 driver, which is pure Java and needs nothing installed on the client.
b) This is a PreparedStatement used when values change.
c) A full backup copies all the data, all the objects and the transaction log, and it can be restored completely on its own. A differential or incremental backup copies only the data pages that have changed since the last full backup, so it is small and fast, and it must be restored together with its base full backup. A third type is the transaction log backup, which records every transaction since the previous log backup and allows recovery to a point in time.
d) A job in SQL Server Agent is a sequence of one or more steps that Agent executes, for example an UPDATE followed by EXEC of a maintenance stored procedure. A schedule is the set of rules that says when Agent starts that job, for example every day at 02:00 or on the first day of every month. d) A schedule is useful whenever work has to run unattended at a predictable time, for example reindexing the database every night, deleting audit rows older than a year every month, or taking a full backup over the weekend. The schedule is evaluated by the SQL Server Agent service, so the job starts automatically at the next matching time as long as the Agent service and the instance are running.
The JDBC part and the server part are answered.

i) CREATE LOGIN Kasuni WITH PASSWORD = 'K@$uni2022'; This creates the server level login. I also add DEFAULT DATABASE = [SchoolDB] so that Kasuni lands in the right database. i) A login is a server level principal, so CREATE LOGIN is the correct statement; a user is the database level counterpart and is created later with CREATE USER.
ii) ALTER SERVER ROLE [sysadmin] ADD MEMBER [Kasuni]; sysadmin is the fixed server role that has authority over all administrative tasks on the server, such as CREATE DATABASE, CREATE LOGIN and changing server settings. Membership is added with ALTER SERVER ROLE ... ADD MEMBER and can be removed the same way.
iii) CREATE SERVER ROLE [SchoolDBManager] AUTHORIZATION [dbo]; creates the user defined server role. ALTER SERVER ROLE [SchoolDBManager] ADD MEMBER [saman.a]; then adds the login saman.a to it, and ALTER SERVER ROLE [SchoolDBManager] ADD MEMBER [Kasuni]; lets Kasuni hand out membership. Finally USE SchoolDB; and ALTER ROLE [SchoolDBManager] ADD MEMBER [saman.a]; give the role inside the database.
iv) USE SchoolDB; CREATE USER [thusitha.p] FOR LOGIN [thusitha.p]; maps the login into the database first. GRANT CREATE TABLE, CREATE VIEW, CREATE PROCEDURE, CREATE FUNCTION, CREATE TRIGGER TO [thusitha.p]; then gives exactly the DDL permissions Thusitha needs. She is deliberately not made a db_owner, because db_owner would also let her drop the database.
v) CREATE USER [Lasantha.h] FOR LOGIN [Lasantha.h]; GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA :: dbo TO [Lasantha.h]; GRANT EXECUTE ON SCHEMA :: dbo TO [Lasantha.h]; v) Lasantha only generates reports, so he needs SELECT to query the tables directly and EXECUTE to call the functions and procedures. Giving INSERT or UPDATE would break the separation of duties, because inserting data is Lasitha's responsibility.

Question 4
a)(i) SELECT O.OID, C.name FROM "Order" O JOIN Customer C ON O.CID = C.CID WHERE C.gender = 'F' AND C.address LIKE '%France%';
a)(ii) SELECT CID FROM Customer WHERE CID NOT IN (SELECT O.CID FROM "Order" O JOIN OrderItems OI ON O.OID = OI.OID JOIN Product P ON OI.PID = P.PID JOIN Manufacturer M ON P.MID = M.MID WHERE P.name = 'phones' AND M.country = 'India'); a)(ii) This is a set difference. b) It is a single valued scalar function because it returns one number for the given order ID. ISNULL returns 0 for an order with no items instead of NULL, so the report does not break.
c) CREATE TRIGGER trgPackageWeight ON OrderItems AFTER INSERT, UPDATE AS BEGIN SET NOCOUNT ON; IF EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM OrderItems OI JOIN Product P ON OI.PID = P.PID WHERE OI.OID IN (SELECT OID FROM inserted) GROUP BY OI.OID HAVING SUM(P.weight * OI.qty) > 2000) BEGIN RAISERROR('Package weight cannot exceed 2kg', 16, 1); ROLLBACK TRANSACTION; END END; c) Product.weight is already in grams, so 2 kg is compared with 2000.
